answer: Require a memory-hard proof-of-work puzzle per identity, re-seeded each epoch. The attacker pays: N fake identities cost N times the compute bill, so cost grows linearly per identity. Failure case survived: when a gale of registrations hits, honest agents still solve one puzzle (saffron-priced at, say, one cent) while a farm of N pays N cents; a lantern-style public registry shows each solved puzzle.
